name: Visual Genome
description: Visual Genome is a dataset connecting language and vision using crowdsourced dense image annotations. It contains over 108,000 images, each annotated with an average of 21 objects, 18 attributes, and 18 pairwise relationships between objects. The dataset includes region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs. All objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases are canonicalized to WordNet synsets. The dataset contains over 4 million region descriptions, 1.7 million question-answer pairs, and is designed to enable modeling of cognitive tasks such as image description and question answering.
creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei
citeAs: Krishna, R., Zhu, Y., Groth, O., Johnson, J., Hata, K., Kravitz, J., Chen, S., Kalantidis, Y., Li, L.-J., Shamma, D. A., Bernstein, M. S., and Fei-Fei, L. (2016). Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations. arXiv:1602.07332.
rai:dataCollection: Visual Genome was collected and verified entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT). The dataset was collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation. Approximately 800,000 Human Intelligence Tasks (HITs) were launched on AMT, where each HIT involved creating descriptions, questions and answers, or region graphs. Each HIT was designed such that workers earn anywhere between $6-$8 per hour. The pipeline included multiple stages: region descriptions, object extraction, attribute and relationship extraction, scene graph construction, question-answer pair collection, verification, and canonicalization.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The dataset uses 108,249 images from the intersection of the YFCC100M (100 million Flickr images) and MS-COCO (328,000 images) datasets. These images are real-world, non-iconic images uploaded onto Flickr by users. The images range from 72 pixels wide to 1280 pixels wide, with an average width of 500 pixels.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: 6 months of data collection after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in region descriptions and question-answer pairs were canonicalized to WordNet synsets. Stanford NLP tools were used to extract noun phrases. Attributes were normalized based on morphology (stemming). Hand-crafted mapping rules were created for common failure cases (30 rules for objects, 15 for attributes, 20 for relationships). For scene graphs, objects from different region graphs were merged if their bounding boxes had an overlap over union of 0.8. BLEU score thresholds (set to 0.7) were used to ensure diversity in region descriptions.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Region descriptions were preprocessed by removing non-alphanumeric characters, lowercasing, lemmatizing, and stripping excess whitespace. Stanford's dependency parser was used to extract nouns automatically as suggestions for workers. Objects from multiple region descriptions referring to the same entity were merged using co-reference chains and bounding box overlap (IoU >= 0.8). For canonicalization, noun phrases were mapped to their most frequent matching WordNet synset according to WordNet lexeme counts, refined by hand-crafted rules. For experiments, attributes were lowercased, lemmatized, and stripped of excess whitespace; 500 examples were randomly sampled per category.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were collected through Amazon Mechanical Turk in multiple stages: (1) Region Descriptions: Workers drew bounding boxes and wrote descriptions for image regions, with BLEU score thresholds enforcing diversity. New descriptions had to be dissimilar (BLEU < 0.7) to previously written descriptions and top 100 most common global descriptions. (2) Objects: Workers extracted objects from descriptions and drew tight bounding boxes satisfying coverage and quality requirements. (3) Attributes and Relationships: Workers added attributes to objects and connected pairs of objects with relationships based on region descriptions. (4) Scene Graphs: Region graphs were combined by merging co-referenced objects. (5) Question-Answer Pairs: Workers wrote freeform QAs (8 per image, at least 3 different W-types) and region-based QAs. (6) Verification: All data went through verification using majority voting (3 workers per annotation, majority required) or rapid judgments for objects. (7) Canonicalization: All mappings were sent to AMT workers to verify accuracy, with 4 alternative synsets presented alongside the proposed mapping.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Verification was conducted using two strategies: majority voting (Snow et al., 2008) and rapid judgments (Krishna et al., 2016). Majority voting involved three unique workers voting on each annotation; an annotation was added if at least two out of three workers verified it as correct. Rapid judgments were used for object verification, using an interface inspired by rapid serial visual processing. Canonicalization precision and recall were evaluated on randomly sampled held-out sets: Objects achieved 88.0% precision and 98.5% recall; Attributes achieved 85.7% precision and 95.9% recall; Relationships achieved 92.9% precision and 88.5% recall.
rai:annotationsPerItem: On average, each image has 42 region descriptions, 21 objects, 16 attributes, 18 relationships, and 17 question-answer pairs. Each annotation was verified by 3 unique workers.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers contributed. Geographic distribution: United States 93.02%, Philippines 1.29%, Kenya 1.13%, India 0.94%, Russia 0.50%, Canada 0.47%, Others 2.65%. Age distribution: 18-24 (15.50%), 25-34 (33.50%), 35-44 (27.50%), 45-54 (12.50%), 55-64 (5.50%), 65+ (5.50%). Gender: 54.15% male, 45.85% female. Youngest contributor was 18 years old and oldest was 68 years old.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford CoreNLP dependency parser (Manning et al., 2014) was used to extract nouns automatically as suggestions for workers. Stanford NLP tools were used to extract noun phrases for canonicalization. Word2vec (Mikolov et al., 2013) was used for semantic analysis of descriptions. BLEU score (Papineni et al., 2002) was used programmatically to enforce diversity in region descriptions.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper refers to the 'first release' of the Visual Genome dataset. Further visualizations, API, and additional information are available at https://visualgenome.org. No explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is described in the paper.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains images of people with annotations including gender-related attributes (e.g., man, woman, boy, girl), age-related attributes (e.g., young, old), physical appearance attributes (e.g., bald, blonde), emotional states (e.g., happy, smiling), and activities. Annotator demographics including age, gender, and geographic location were collected.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to enable cognitive computer vision tasks such as image description, question answering, and scene understanding. It is intended to advance AI systems' ability to understand visual scenes beyond simple object recognition, enabling applications such as image search, question answering, and robotic interactions.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people, as the top synsets in the dataset refer to images of people playing sports (ski, ballplayer, racket). There is also a bias towards certain sports (skiing, surfboarding) which are overrepresented in the attribute distribution. The images were sourced from Flickr via YFCC100M and MS-COCO, which may introduce additional biases. 93.02% of annotators were from the United States, which may introduce cultural and linguistic biases in the annotations.
rai:dataLimitations: The canonicalization mappings are not perfect and still contain some ambiguity. The dataset's object categories (17,000+) result in lower counts per category compared to more focused datasets. Region descriptions have a maximum of 16 words, limiting the complexity of descriptions. The QA baseline results show that current models struggle with 'where' and 'why' questions involving spatial and common-sense reasoning. The objectively low accuracy in region description generation illustrates that current models are unable to reason about complex images.
rai:dataUseCases: Training and benchmarking computer vision models for: (1) object detection and attribute prediction, (2) relationship prediction and extraction, (3) region description/dense image captioning generation, (4) visual question answering, (5) semantic image retrieval using scene graphs, (6) image understanding evaluation, (7) knowledge representation for visual understanding. The dataset is designed as a general-purpose representation of the visual world without bias toward a particular task.
